text:
Jordan Kyrou's first season in Washington, after the Blues traded him for Connor McMichael and a first-round pick, has come with a much smaller job. He plays 14.6 minutes a night, and his own chance quality has dropped to 0.53 expected goals per 60 minutes, about half of last season's 1.00 (expected goals measure the quality of chances).

His numbers pull in two directions. He has 5 goals on 2.3 expected, shooting 19% after 10% last season, so his finishing is running hot. But the Capitals have scored 6.4 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, which has cost him assists. He has 14 points in 18 games and has gone pointless in his last four.

Last season showed a fuller player. Evolving-Hockey had him 58th of 401 forwards, driving offense at the 96th percentile and taking chances away at the 99th. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting 7.7 scoring chances per 60 from right in front of the net, 95th percentile. The question for Washington is whether that version gets more ice. Watch his minutes and his chances in front.
headline: Kyrou's new role in Washington is smaller
